\section[\texorpdfstring{\ta{தெம்பு} (tempu)}{தெம்பு (tempu)}]{\ta{தெம்பு} (tempu) — vigour; energy}

\label{lesson:TA-C468-tempu}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for to babble, then the Tamil for to tickle.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{தெம்பு}}
\textbf{\ta{தெம்பு}} — \emph{tempu} — \textquotedblleft{}vigour; energy\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ta{சாப்பிட்ட} \ta{பிறகு} \ta{எனக்குத்} \ta{தெம்பு} \ta{வந்தது}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{cāppiṭṭa piṟaku eṉakkut tempu vantatu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
After eating I got my strength back.
\end{quote}

\ta{தெம்பாக} \ta{இருக்கிறது}, I feel strong.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ta{தெம்பு}} (\emph{tempu}) is native Dravidian (DEDR 3416); Telugu has the same word for boldness.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tempu}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tempu}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{cāppiṭṭa piṟaku eṉakkut tempu vantatu.} — After eating I got my strength back.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for to babble, then the Tamil for to tickle, then say \emph{tempu} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ta{தெம்பு} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Vigour; energy\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ta{சலி} (cali)}{சலி (cali)}]{\ta{சலி} (cali) — to tire of}

\label{lesson:TA-C468-cali}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for to tickle, then the Tamil for vigour.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{சலி}}
\textbf{\ta{சலி}} — \emph{cali} — \textquotedblleft{}to tire of\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ta{நீண்ட} \ta{பயணத்தில்} \ta{எனக்குச்} \ta{சலித்துவிட்டது}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{nīṇṭa payaṇattil eṉakkuc calittuviṭṭatu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I grew tired on the long journey.
\end{quote}

Past (it …): \ta{சலித்தது}, \emph{calittatu}.

Dative experiencer, past \ta{சலித்தது}. Not \ta{சலி} \textquotedblleft{}to sift\textquotedblright{}, which DEDR keeps apart.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ta{சலி}} (\emph{cali}) is native Dravidian (DEDR 2371). DEDR keeps \ta{சலி} \textquotedblleft{}to sift\textquotedblright{} as a separate entry (2370).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{cali}, once more

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ta{துவள்} (tuvaḷ)}{துவள் (tuvaḷ)}]{\ta{துவள்} (tuvaḷ) — to droop; to go limp}

\label{lesson:TA-C468-tuval}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for vigour, then the Tamil for to tire of.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{துவள்}}
\textbf{\ta{துவள்}} — \emph{tuvaḷ} — \textquotedblleft{}to droop; to go limp\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ta{வெயிலில்} \ta{வேலை} \ta{செய்து} \ta{அவர்} \ta{துவண்டார்}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{veyilil vēlai ceytu avar tuvaṇṭār.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Working in the sun, he wilted.
\end{quote}

Past (I …): \ta{துவண்டேன்}, \emph{tuvaṇṭēṉ}.

Past \ta{துவண்டேன்}, with \ta{ள்} + \ta{ந்} written \ta{ண்ட}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ta{துவள்}} (\emph{tuvaḷ}) is native Dravidian: DEDR 3354 lists it with the sense \textquotedblleft{}to quiver, to tremble\textquotedblright{}; the modern sense is drooping with weakness.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tuvaḷ}, once more

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for vigour, then the Tamil for to tire of, then say \emph{tuvaḷ} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ta{தளர்} (taḷar)}{தளர் (taḷar)}]{\ta{தளர்} (taḷar) — to weaken; to slacken}

\label{lesson:TA-C468-talar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for to tire of, then the Tamil for to droop.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{தளர்}}
\textbf{\ta{தளர்}} — \emph{taḷar} — \textquotedblleft{}to weaken; to slacken\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ta{வயதான} \ta{பிறகு} \ta{தாத்தாவின்} \ta{உடல்} \ta{தளர்ந்தது}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{vayatāṉa piṟaku tāttāviṉ uṭal taḷarntatu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
As he grew old, grandfather’s body weakened.
\end{quote}

Past (I …): \ta{தளர்ந்தேன்}, \emph{taḷarntēṉ}.

\ta{தளர்வான} \textquotedblleft{}loose\textquotedblright{} comes from the same verb.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ta{தளர்}} (\emph{taḷar}) is native Dravidian (DEDR 3127), of tired limbs, slack ropes and old age.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{taḷar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{vayatāṉa piṟaku tāttāviṉ uṭal taḷarntatu.} — As he grew old, grandfather’s body weakened.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for to tire of, then the Tamil for to droop, then say \emph{taḷar} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ta{கண்ணயர்} (kaṇṇayar)}{கண்ணயர் (kaṇṇayar)}]{\ta{கண்ணயர்} (kaṇṇayar) — to nod off; to doze}

\label{lesson:TA-C468-kannayar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for to droop, then the Tamil for to weaken.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{கண்ணயர்}}
\textbf{\ta{கண்ணயர்}} — \emph{kaṇṇayar} — \textquotedblleft{}to nod off; to doze\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ta{பேருந்தில்} \ta{உட்கார்ந்ததும்} \ta{நான்} \ta{கண்ணயர்ந்தேன்}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{pēruntil uṭkārntatum nāṉ kaṇṇayarntēṉ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
As soon as I sat down in the bus, I nodded off.
\end{quote}

Past (I …): \ta{கண்ணயர்ந்தேன்}, \emph{kaṇṇayarntēṉ}.

\ta{கண்} \textquotedblleft{}eye\textquotedblright{} + \ta{அயர்} \textquotedblleft{}to grow weary\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ta{கண்ணயர்}} (\emph{kaṇṇayar}) is a native compound of \ta{கண்} \emph{kaṇ}, \textquotedblleft{}eye\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 1159), and \ta{அயர்} \emph{ayar}, \textquotedblleft{}to lose consciousness, to grow weary\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 39).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for to droop, then the Tamil for to weaken, then say \emph{kaṇṇayar} again
\end{itemize}

\section[(dialogue)]{Looking back: from Patience and Eagerness to Energy and Weariness}

\label{lesson:TA-R468-review-461-468}



\begin{quote}
Say the Tamil for patience and composure.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item patience, composure, to tolerate, keenness, eagerness
  \item humiliation, awkwardness, bashfulness, disgust, to grimace
  \item grief, torment, suffering, emptiness, condolence
  \item temptation, despair, a nuisance, to plead, to be fed up
  \item to long for, family affection, fondness, infatuation, to be moved
  \item courage, a coward, to dread, to cower, to threaten
  \item teasing, naughtiness, to nag, to babble, to tickle
  \item vigour, to tire of, to droop, to weaken, to nod off
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Patience? (\textbf{\ta{பொறுமை}}, \emph{poṟumai}.) Composure? (\textbf{\ta{நிதானம்}}, \emph{nitāṉam}.) To tolerate? (\textbf{\ta{சகி}}, \emph{caki}.) Keenness? (\textbf{\ta{ஆர்வம்}}, \emph{ārvam}.) Eagerness? (\textbf{\ta{ஆவல்}}, \emph{āval}.) Humiliation? (\textbf{\ta{அவமானம்}}, \emph{avamāṉam}.) Awkwardness? (\textbf{\ta{சங்கடம்}}, \emph{caṅkaṭam}.) Bashfulness? (\textbf{\ta{கூச்சம்}}, \emph{kūccam}.) Disgust? (\textbf{\ta{அருவருப்பு}}, \emph{aruvaruppu}.) To grimace? (\textbf{\ta{முகம்} \ta{சுளி}}, \emph{mukam cuḷi}.) Grief? (\textbf{\ta{துக்கம்}}, \emph{tukkam}.) Torment? (\textbf{\ta{வேதனை}}, \emph{vētaṉai}.) Suffering? (\textbf{\ta{துன்பம்}}, \emph{tuṉpam}.) Emptiness? (\textbf{\ta{வெறுமை}}, \emph{veṟumai}.) Condolence? (\textbf{\ta{இரங்கல்}}, \emph{iraṅkal}.) Temptation? (\textbf{\ta{சபலம்}}, \emph{capalam}.) Despair? (\textbf{\ta{விரக்தி}}, \emph{virakti}.) A nuisance? (\textbf{\ta{தொந்தரவு}}, \emph{tontaravu}.) To plead? (\textbf{\ta{மன்றாடு}}, \emph{maṉṟāṭu}.) To be fed up? (\textbf{\ta{அலு}}, \emph{alu}.) To long for? (\textbf{\ta{ஏங்கு}}, \emph{ēṅku}.) Family affection? (\textbf{\ta{பாசம்}}, \emph{pācam}.) Fondness? (\textbf{\ta{பிரியம்}}, \emph{piriyam}.) Infatuation? (\textbf{\ta{மோகம்}}, \emph{mōkam}.) To be moved? (\textbf{\ta{நெகிழ்}}, \emph{nekiḻ}.) Courage? (\textbf{\ta{துணிச்சல்}}, \emph{tuṇiccal}.) A coward? (\textbf{\ta{கோழை}}, \emph{kōḻai}.) To dread? (\textbf{\ta{அஞ்சு}}, \emph{añcu}.) To cower? (\textbf{\ta{பதுங்கு}}, \emph{patuṅku}.) To threaten? (\textbf{\ta{மிரட்டு}}, \emph{miraṭṭu}.) Teasing? (\textbf{\ta{கிண்டல்}}, \emph{kiṇṭal}.) Naughtiness? (\textbf{\ta{சேட்டை}}, \emph{cēṭṭai}.) To nag? (\textbf{\ta{நச்சரி}}, \emph{naccari}.) To babble? (\textbf{\ta{உளறு}}, \emph{uḷaṟu}.) To tickle? (\textbf{\ta{குறுகுறு}}, \emph{kuṟukuṟu}.) Vigour? (\textbf{\ta{தெம்பு}}, \emph{tempu}.) To tire of? (\textbf{\ta{சலி}}, \emph{cali}.) To droop? (\textbf{\ta{துவள்}}, \emph{tuvaḷ}.) To weaken? (\textbf{\ta{தளர்}}, \emph{taḷar}.) To nod off? (\textbf{\ta{கண்ணயர்}}, \emph{kaṇṇayar}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
